procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 29.03.2010 in CWP No.18290 of 2009
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh issued a Judgment and Order on 29.03.2010 in CWP No.18290 of 2009.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Supreme Court was approached, resulting in Civil Appeal No. 2317 of 2011. The Supreme Court ultimately referred the matter to a larger bench for consideration of certain aspects, to be determined by the Chief Justice on the administrative side.

cases.case_name: Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India
cases.principle: In examining provisions of the Constitution, courts should adopt the primary rule, and give effect to the plain meaning of the expressions; this rule can be departed from only when there are ambiguities.
For the rule of constitutional interpretation that courts should give effect to the plain meaning of expressions, a principle later quoted and applied in the Kuldip Nayar case.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The law established by the Five-Judge Bench in E.V. Chinnaiah is affirmed as correct. Interrelated constitutional provisions, specifically fundamental rights, must be interpreted in light of the directive principles, which should serve as a code of interpretation for the courts.
obiter: The doctrines of binding precedent and stare decisis are of utmost importance to the judicial system, promoting certainty and consistency, and require that decisions of a larger bench be followed by a smaller bench.

While constitutional provisions may be given a broad and generous construction, the rule of “plain meaning” or “literal” interpretation remains the primary and safe rule, unless the language is contradictory, ambiguous, or leads to absurd results.
Every word or expression used in the Constitution has a purpose.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Court, in view of the matter, referred the case for consideration by a larger Bench, directing that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice on the administrative side for an appropriate order.
legal_tests_applied: A reference to a larger Bench is only appropriate when a proposition is contradicted by a subsequent judgment of the same Bench, or it is shown that the proposition laid down has become unworkable or contrary to a well-established principle.
When the State creates a sub-class for preferential treatment, it must justify the classification on the basis of empirical data.
policy_considerations: The doctrines of Precedents and Stare decisis are the core values of our legal system.
When a decision is rendered by this Court, it acquires a reliance interest and the society organises itself based on such legal order.

When substantial judicial time and resources are spent on the References by the Constitution Benches, the same should not be further referred to the larger Bench by a smaller Bench, in a casual or cavalier manner, and without recording the reasons for disagreement.
The purpose of a law may be either the elimination of a public mischief or the achievement of some positive public good.
